title: Dual-horizon coalescing scheduler with KV residency forecast
creator: Priya Rao
description:
Problem: Our continuous batcher shows degraded throughput and elevated tail latency for mixed prompt/response workloads where short prompts are followed by very long responses (e.g., summarization + long streaming). The current slot coalescing favors immediate packing which increases KV residency and GPU memory pressure, causing frequent evictions and kernel slowdown.

Goal: Implement a dual-horizon coalescing scheduler that separates short-term coalescing (latency-first) from medium-horizon coalescing (throughput-first) combined with a lightweight KV residency forecast to make eviction decisions that reduce tail latency and total memory churn. Deliver measurable improvements on mixed-length production traces without increasing median latency beyond current SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end integration in the continuous batcher runtime with a feature flag
Tail P95 latency for mixed-length benchmark reduced by at least 18% vs baseline
Ordered KV eviction events reduced by >30% on production replay over 7d
No more than 5% regression in median latency for short single-turn prompts
Automated canary dashboards added to Console with route-level breakdowns
tasks: Design dual-horizon policy and write spec (scheduler horizon parameters, aging watermark)
Prototype KV residency forecast model (lightweight exponential moving average based on slot age + seq length)
Implement scheduler integration and interrupt-safe coalescing path
Add memory compaction window and soft-eviction hooks to runtime
Build microbench harness for mixed-length traces and synthetic long-response workloads
Run 7d production-replay test, collect KV eviction, GPU memory footprint, and latency histograms
Create Console dashboard tiles and alert queries for regressions
Open PR(s) and iterate on perf review feedback
decisions: Use two horizons: immediate (<=30ms hold) for latency-sensitive coalescing and medium (<=120ms hold) for throughput aggregation
Forecast model will be heuristic EMAs (slot age, recent sequence-length distribution) rather than ML model to keep CPU overhead minimal
Eviction strategy: prefer compacting cold prefixes first, avoid killing hot KV banks unless memory pressure exceeds high watermark
Expose horizon and forecast parameters behind runtime feature flag for controlled rollouts
tradeoffs: Longer coalescing horizon increases throughput but risks higher median latency for short requests; mitigated by dual-horizon approach
Lightweight forecast avoids compute overhead but may mispredict rare traffic spikes compared to a trained model
Soft eviction + compaction reduces interruptions but increases implementation complexity and surface area for bugs
risks: Incorrect forecast tuning could delay eviction and trigger OOMs under pathological bursts
Complex scheduler state increases chance of deadlocks or race conditions during shutdown or preemption
Canary signals may not catch workload patterns present only in a subset of customers
